cor-alternating-forms-one-dimensional.title: Alternating n-Forms on F^n Form a Line
cor-alternating-forms-one-dimensional.title_html: Alternating n-Forms on Fn Form a Line
cor-alternating-forms-one-dimensional.html: The vector space of alternating n-linear forms on Fn has dimension 1, with basis (det). Explicitly, every alternating n-linear form f on Fn satisfies f(a1,…,an)=f(e1,…,en)det(a1,…,an).

cor-det-inverse.title: Determinant of the Inverse
cor-det-inverse.html: If A∈Mn(F) is invertible, then detA≠0 and det(A−1)=(detA)−1.

cor-det-similarity-invariant.title: Determinant Is a Similarity Invariant
cor-det-similarity-invariant.html: If A,B∈Mn(F) are similar, then detA=detB.

cor-gram-determinant-nonnegative.title: Gram Determinants Are Non-negative
cor-gram-determinant-nonnegative.html: Let A∈Mm×n(R). Then det(AA⊤)=∑S⊆[n]|S|=m(detA[m],S)2 ≥ 0, with equality if and only if rankA<m.

cor-integer-inverse.title: Integer Matrices with Integer Inverses
cor-integer-inverse.html:
Let A∈Mn(Q) have all entries in Z.

  1. detA∈Z, and adjA has all entries in Z.
  2. A is invertible and A−1 has all entries in Z if and only if detA=1 or detA=−1.

cor-inverse-formula.title: Inverse via the Adjugate
cor-inverse-formula.html: Let A∈Mn(F) with detA≠0. Then A is invertible and A−1=1detAadjA.

cor-parity-well-defined.title: Parity Is Well Defined
cor-parity-well-defined.html: Let n≥2 and σ∈Sn. If σ=τ1⋯τr is a product of r transpositions, then sgnσ=(−1)r. Consequently, if also σ=τ1′⋯τs′ with transpositions τm′, then r and s are both even or both odd.

cor-sign-transposition.title: Sign of a Transposition
cor-sign-transposition.html: Every transposition is odd: sgn(i j)=−1 for all i≠j in {1,…,n}.

cor-vandermonde-nonzero.title: Distinct Nodes Give an Invertible Vandermonde Matrix
cor-vandermonde-nonzero.title_html: Distinct Nodes Give an Invertible Vandermonde Matrix
cor-vandermonde-nonzero.html: V(x1,…,xn) is invertible if and only if x1,…,xn are distinct.

def-adjugate.title: Adjugate
def-adjugate.html: Let n≥2 and A∈Mn(F). The adjugate of A is the matrix adjA∈Mn(F) with entries (adjA)ij:=Cji, that is, the transpose of the matrix (Cij) of cofactors. For n=1 we set adjA:=(1).

def-alternating-form.title: Alternating Form
def-alternating-form.html: A k-linear form f:Vk→F is alternating if f(v1,…,vk)=0 whenever vi=vj for some pair of positions i≠j.

def-alternating-group.title: Alternating Group
def-alternating-group.html: The alternating group An is the kernel of sgn:Sn→{1,−1}, that is, the subgroup of even permutations in Sn.

def-characteristic-polynomial.title: Characteristic Polynomial
def-characteristic-polynomial.html: Let n≥1 and A=(aij)∈Mn(F). The characteristic polynomial of A is pA(x):=det(xIn−A)=∑σ∈Snsgn(σ)∏j=1n(xδσ(j)j−aσ(j)j) ∈F[x], where δij=1 if i=j and 0 otherwise, so that xδij−aij is the (i,j)-entry of xIn−A. The determinant is the Leibniz sum of @def-determinant, computed in the commutative ring F[x].

def-charpoly-operator.title: Characteristic Polynomial of an Operator
def-charpoly-operator.html: Let V be a vector space over F with dim⁡V=n≥1, and let T∈L(V). The characteristic polynomial of T is pT(x):=p[T]B(x)=det(xIn−[T]B), where B is any basis of V.

def-det-operator.title: Determinant of an operator
def-det-operator.html: Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over F with dim⁡V≥1, and let T∈L(V). The determinant of T is detT:=det[T]B, where B is any basis of V. For V={0} we set detT=1.

def-determinant.title: Determinant
def-determinant.html: Let n≥1 and A=(aij)∈Mn(F). The determinant of A is detA:=∑σ∈Snsgn(σ)aσ(1)1aσ(2)2⋯aσ(n)n ∈F. For columns a1,…,an∈Fn we also write det(a1,…,an) for the determinant of the matrix (a1⋯an).

def-inversion.title: Inversion
def-inversion.html: Let σ∈Sn. An inversion of σ is a pair (i,j) of positions with 1≤i<j≤n and σ(i)>σ(j). We write inv(σ) for the number of inversions of σ.

def-minor-cofactor.title: Minor and cofactor
def-minor-cofactor.html: Let n≥2, A∈Mn(F) and i,j∈{1,…,n}. The (i,j)-minor of A is Mij:=det(the (n−1)×(n−1) matrix obtained from Aby deleting row i and column j). The (i,j)-cofactor of A is Cij:=(−1)i+jMij.

def-multilinear-form.title: Multilinear Form
def-multilinear-form.html: A function f:Vk→F is k-linear, or a multilinear form on V, if for every position i∈{1,…,k} and every choice of v1,…,vi−1,vi+1,…,vk∈V, the function V→F,x↦f(v1,…,vi−1,x,vi+1,…,vk) is linear. A 2-linear form is called bilinear.

def-orientation.title: Orientation
def-orientation.html: Let V be a vector space over R with dim⁡V=n≥1, and let B and C be ordered bases of V. We say B and C have the same orientation if det[id]BC>0, and opposite orientations if det[id]BC<0.

def-parallelepiped-volume.title: Volume of a Parallelepiped
def-parallelepiped-volume.html: Let n≥1 and a1,…,an∈Rn. The (n-dimensional) volume of the parallelepiped spanned by a1,…,an is vol(a1,…,an):=|det(a1a2⋯an)| ≥0.

def-sign-permutation.title: Sign of a Permutation
def-sign-permutation.html: The sign of σ∈Sn is sgnσ=(−1)inv(σ)∈{1,−1}. The permutation σ is even if sgnσ=1 and odd if sgnσ=−1.

def-skew-symmetric-form.title: Skew-Symmetric Form
def-skew-symmetric-form.html: A k-linear form f:Vk→F is skew-symmetric if, for all v1,…,vk∈V and all positions i<j, swapping the arguments in positions i and j multiplies the value by −1: f(v1,…,vj,…,vi,…,vk)=−f(v1,…,vi,…,vj,…,vk), where on the left vj sits in position i, vi sits in position j, and all other positions are unchanged.

def-submatrix-minor.title: Submatrix and Minor
def-submatrix-minor.html: Let A=(aij)∈Mm×n(F), and let 1≤k≤min(m,n). Let I={i1<i2<⋯<ik}⊆[m] and J={j1<j2<⋯<jk}⊆[n] be sets with exactly k elements each, listed in increasing order. The submatrix of A on rows I and columns J is AI,J:=(aipjq)p,q=1k∈Mk(F), the k×k matrix whose (p,q)-entry is aipjq. Its determinant detAI,J is a k×k minor of A.

exm-all-ones-perturbed.title: a on the Diagonal, 1 Elsewhere
exm-all-ones-perturbed.title_html: a on the Diagonal, 1 Elsewhere
exm-all-ones-perturbed.html: Let a∈R and n≥1, and let An∈Mn(R) have every diagonal entry a and every other entry 1. Find detAn.

exm-alternating-forms.title: Alternating Forms
exm-alternating-forms.html:
Check that each of the following is an alternating form.

  1. On F2, for a fixed c∈F: fc(u,v)=c(u1v2−u2v1).
  2. On F3, for fixed coordinate indices 1≤r<s≤3: grs(u,v)=urvs−usvr.
  3. On F[x]: h(p,q)=p(0)q(1)−p(1)q(0).
  4. On any V, with k=1: any linear functional φ∈V∗.

exm-cauchy-binet.title: Cauchy–Binet for a 2 \times 3 times 3 \times 2 Product
exm-cauchy-binet.title_html: Cauchy–Binet for a 2×3 times 3×2 Product
exm-cauchy-binet.html: Let A=(120013),B=(10112−1) over Q. Compute det(AB) directly and by the Cauchy–Binet formula. Then compute det(BA).

exm-charpoly-operators.title: Characteristic Polynomials of Two Operators
exm-charpoly-operators.html: On V=R[x]≤2, find the characteristic polynomials of differentiation D(q)=q′ and of the shift S(q)(x)=q(x+1).

exm-charpoly-small.title: A 3 \times 3 Characteristic Polynomial
exm-charpoly-small.title_html: A 3×3 Characteristic Polynomial
exm-charpoly-small.html: Find pA for A=(201131102)∈M3(Q).

exm-det-by-elimination.title: A 4 \times 4 Determinant by Elimination
exm-det-by-elimination.title_html: A 4×4 Determinant by Elimination
exm-det-by-elimination.html: Compute detA for A=(024211032315−1231)∈M4(R).

exm-laplace-4x4.title: A 4 \times 4 Expansion
exm-laplace-4x4.title_html: A 4×4 Expansion
exm-laplace-4x4.html: Compute detA for A=(3102102024130152)∈M4(R) by expanding along a suitable row.

exm-rank-by-minors.title: Rank of a Family of Matrices
exm-rank-by-minors.title_html: Rank of a Family of Matrices
exm-rank-by-minors.html: For t∈Q, let A(t)=(1212t336t). Find rankA(t) for every t.

exm-sign-two-ways.title: A Sign Computed Two Ways
exm-sign-two-ways.html: Find the sign of the permutation σ∈S6 with two-line notation (123456453621), first by counting inversions and then from its cycles.

exm-tridiagonal-fibonacci.title: Fibonacci Numbers as Determinants
exm-tridiagonal-fibonacci.html: Let Tn have 1 on the diagonal, 1 above it and −1 below it. Find Dn=detTn.

exm-two-by-two-from-rules.title: ad - bc from the Rules
exm-two-by-two-from-rules.title_html: ad−bc from the Rules
exm-two-by-two-from-rules.html: Let D:R2×R2→R be any function satisfying (R1)–(R4). Show that D((a,c),(b,d))=ad−bc for all a,b,c,d∈R.

exm-vandermonde-three.title: A 3 \times 3 Vandermonde Determinant
exm-vandermonde-three.title_html: A 3×3 Vandermonde Determinant
exm-vandermonde-three.html: Compute detV(1,2,4) from the formula and by cofactor expansion.

exm-volume-scaling.title: Area of an Image
exm-volume-scaling.html: Let T:R2→R2 be T(x,y)=(3x+y, x+2y). Find the area of the image of the unit square, and of the image of the parallelogram P((1,1),(−1,2)).

exr-area-and-volume-a1.title: A1
exr-area-and-volume-a1.html:
1. State the four rules (R1)–(R4) for signed area.
  2. True or false: ordinary (unsigned) area satisfies area(u,v+w)=area(u,v)+area(u,w) for all u,v,w∈R2. Justify your answer.
  3. Find the signed area of P((1,3),(2,4)). Is (1234) invertible?
  4. Explain why any D satisfying (R1) and (R2) has D(u,5u)=0.
  5. How many terms does the full expansion for 4×4 matrices have, and how many products does the 4×4 analogue of Sarrus’s rule use?

exr-area-and-volume-b1.title: B1: Signed Areas from the Rules
exr-area-and-volume-b1.title_html: B1: Signed Areas from the Rules
exr-area-and-volume-b1.html:
Using only (R1)–(R4), in the manner of @exm-two-by-two-from-rules, compute the following. Then check each answer against ad−bc.

  1. D((2,1),(4,5)).
  2. D((1,2),(3,6)).
  3. D((0,3),(2,0)).

exr-area-and-volume-b2.title: B2: Equal Sides Force the Swap Rule
exr-area-and-volume-b2.title_html: B2: Equal Sides Force the Swap Rule
exr-area-and-volume-b2.html:
Let D:R2×R2→R satisfy (R1), (R3) and (R5), but not necessarily (R2).

  1. Prove that D(u,v)=−D(v,u) for all u,v∈R2.
  2. Suppose moreover that (R4) holds. Deduce that D((a,c),(b,d))=ad−bc.

Hint: expand D(u+v,u+v).

exr-area-and-volume-c1.title: C1: Area of a Triangle
exr-area-and-volume-c1.html:
Let p,q,r∈R2.

  1. Explain why the triangle with vertices p,q,r has area 12|D(q−p,r−p)|, where D(u,v) is the signed area.
  2. Find the area of the triangle with vertices (1,2), (4,3), (2,6).
  3. Hence decide whether the points (0,1), (2,4), (6,10) lie on a line. Justify your answer.

exr-area-and-volume-c2.title: C2: The 1 \times 1 Case
exr-area-and-volume-c2.title_html: C2: The 1×1 Case
exr-area-and-volume-c2.html:
For n=1, the rules ask for a function f:F→F of one vector in F1=F.

  1. Explain why the rule “zero whenever two arguments are equal” imposes no condition when n=1.
  2. Prove that the only function f:F→F that is linear with f(1)=1 is f(a)=a. Hence the determinant of a 1×1 matrix (a) must be a.

exr-characteristic-polynomial-a1.title: A1
exr-characteristic-polynomial-a1.html:
1. Define the characteristic polynomial of A∈Mn(F), and say in which ring its determinant is computed.
  2. State the degree, leading coefficient, coefficient of xn−1 and constant term of pA.
  3. True or false: det(A−xI)=pA(x) for every A∈M3(F). Justify your answer.
  4. True or false: if pA=pB, then A∼B. Justify your answer.
  5. What does pA(c)=0 say about the matrix cI−A? About vectors?
  6. Explain in one sentence why “pA(A)=det(AI−A)=0” is not a proof.

exr-characteristic-polynomial-b1.title: B1: Computing characteristic polynomials
exr-characteristic-polynomial-b1.html: Find the characteristic polynomial of each matrix over Q, factor it as far as possible over Q, and check the trace and determinant against @thm-charpoly-coefficients. A=(110011101),B=(210002000013001−1). Hence list the c∈Q for which cI−A, respectively cI−B, is not invertible.

exr-characteristic-polynomial-b2.title: B2: Transpose
exr-characteristic-polynomial-b2.html: Prove that pA⊤=pA for every A∈Mn(F). Hence show that cI−A is invertible if and only if cI−A⊤ is.

exr-characteristic-polynomial-b3.title: B3: \A\B and \B\A
exr-characteristic-polynomial-b3.title_html: B3: AB and BA
exr-characteristic-polynomial-b3.html:
Let A,B∈Mn(F) with A invertible.

  1. Show that BA=A−1(AB)A, and deduce pAB=pBA.
  2. Deduce that tr(AB)=tr(BA) and det(AB)=det(BA) in this case.
  3. Check (a) for A=(1101), B=(0010), and note that AB≠BA.

(Chapter 8 removes the hypothesis that A is invertible.)

exr-characteristic-polynomial-c1.title: C1: Companion matrices
exr-characteristic-polynomial-c1.html:
Let n≥2 and p(x)=xn+an−1xn−1+⋯+a1x+a0∈F[x]. The companion matrix of p is the matrix C(p)∈Mn(F) with 1 in each position (i+1,i) just below the diagonal, last column (−a0,−a1,…,−an−1), and 0 elsewhere: C(p)=(00⋯0−a010⋯0−a101⋯0−a2⋮⋱⋮00⋯1−an−1). (The matrix C of @exr-polynomials-of-operators-b2 is C(x3−2x2+x−2).)

  1. Let M=xI−C(p). For each i, show that deleting row i and column n of M leaves a block diagonal matrix whose blocks are an (i−1)×(i−1) lower triangular matrix with diagonal x,…,x and an (n−i)×(n−i) upper triangular matrix with diagonal −1,…,−1 (either block may be absent when i=1 or i=n). Deduce that the cofactor Cin of M equals xi−1.
  2. Deduce, by expanding along the last column, that pC(p)=p.
  3. Verify (b) for p=x4+x3−2x+3 by writing C(p) and checking the coefficients predicted by @thm-charpoly-coefficients.
  4. Deduce that every monic polynomial of degree n≥1 over F is the characteristic polynomial of some n×n matrix over F.

exr-characteristic-polynomial-c2.title: C2: Nilpotent 2 \times 2 matrices
exr-characteristic-polynomial-c2.title_html: C2: Nilpotent 2×2 matrices
exr-characteristic-polynomial-c2.html:
Let A∈M2(F) satisfy Ak=0 for some k≥1.

  1. Show that the constant term of pA is 0.
  2. By multiplying out, verify that A2−(trA)A+(detA)I=0 for every A∈M2(F).
  3. Deduce that trA=0, and hence pA=x2 and A2=0.
  4. Give an example showing that A2=0 does not force A=0.

exr-characteristic-polynomial-c3.title: C3: Odd size over the reals
exr-characteristic-polynomial-c3.title_html: C3: Odd size over the reals
exr-characteristic-polynomial-c3.html:
Let n be odd and A∈Mn(R).

  1. Prove that there is c∈R and a non-zero v∈Rn with Av=cv.
  2. Show by an example that (a) fails for n=2.
  3. Show that (a) holds for every A∈Mn(C) and every n≥1.

exr-cofactor-expansion-a1.title: A1
exr-cofactor-expansion-a1.html:
1. Define the (i,j)-minor, the (i,j)-cofactor and the adjugate of A∈Mn(F), n≥2.
  2. What are the signs (−1)i+j of the cofactors in positions (2,3) and (4,4)?
  3. True or false: adjA is defined only when A is invertible. Justify your answer.
  4. True or false: Cramer’s rule (@thm-cramers-rule) gives the solutions of every square linear system Ax=b. Justify your answer.
  5. In the proof of @thm-adjugate-identity, which matrix is expanded to show that ∑jaijCkj=0 for i≠k, and why is its determinant 0?
  6. True or false: if A has integer entries and detA=2, then A−1 has integer entries. Justify your answer.

exr-cofactor-expansion-b1.title: B1: Adjugate and inverse
exr-cofactor-expansion-b1.html: Let A=(12−1013211)∈M3(R). Compute all nine cofactors, adjA and detA. Verify that AadjA=(detA)I3, and hence write down A−1.

exr-cofactor-expansion-b2.title: B2: Cramer’s rule
exr-cofactor-expansion-b2.html: Use Cramer’s rule to solve x1+2x2−x3=−3,x2+3x3=5,2x1+x2+x3=3 over R. Check your answer by substitution.

exr-cofactor-expansion-b3.title: B3: Choosing the best line
exr-cofactor-expansion-b3.html: Compute detN for N=(2003140−105023120)∈M4(R), expanding along the row or column that needs the least work.

exr-cofactor-expansion-c1.title: C1: The determinant of the adjugate
exr-cofactor-expansion-c1.title_html: C1: The determinant of the adjugate
exr-cofactor-expansion-c1.html:
Let n≥2 and A∈Mn(F). Prove that det(adjA)=(detA)n−1.

Hint: treat detA≠0 and detA=0 separately; in the second case, ask whether adjA can be invertible.

exr-cofactor-expansion-c2.title: C2: The rank of the adjugate
exr-cofactor-expansion-c2.title_html: C2: The rank of the adjugate
exr-cofactor-expansion-c2.html:
Let n≥2 and A∈Mn(F). Prove that rank(adjA)={nif rankA=n,1if rankA=n−1,0if rankA≤n−2.

  1. Prove the case rankA=n.
  2. Suppose rankA≤n−2. Prove that every minor Mij is 0.
  3. Suppose rankA=n−1. Prove that every column of adjA lies in nul(A), and deduce rank(adjA)≤1.
  4. Suppose rankA=n−1. Prove that some minor Mij is non-zero, and conclude.

Hint for (d): choose n−1 independent columns of A, then n−1 independent rows of the resulting n×(n−1) matrix.

exr-cofactor-expansion-c3.title: C3: An adjugate over F[x]
exr-cofactor-expansion-c3.title_html: C3: An adjugate over F[x]
exr-cofactor-expansion-c3.html:
Work in M2(R[x]), using the remarks after @thm-laplace-expansion and @thm-adjugate-identity.

  1. For A=(1234), compute det(xI−A) and adj(xI−A), and verify (xI−A)adj(xI−A)=det(xI−A)I by multiplying out.
  2. For a general A=(abcd)∈M2(R), show that adj(xI−A)=xI−adjA and A+adjA=(trA)I.
  3. Deduce from (b), without using @thm-adjugate-identity over R[x], that (xI−A)adj(xI−A)=(x2−(trA)x+detA)I, and check that x2−(trA)x+detA=det(xI−A).

exr-existence-and-uniqueness-a1.title: A1
exr-existence-and-uniqueness-a1.html:
1. State the three properties that characterize det:Mn(F)→F, and write down the Leibniz formula.
  2. How many terms does the Leibniz formula have for n=4? How many of the corresponding permutations have sign 1?
  3. True or false: det(A+B)=detA+detB for all A,B∈M2(R). Justify your answer.
  4. True or false: det(−A)=−detA for all A∈M3(R). Justify your answer.
  5. In the proof of @thm-alternating-form-uniqueness, why does a term with a non-injective φ vanish?
  6. Explain why the existence proof pairs σ with σ(p q) instead of arguing “D=−D, so D=0”.

exr-existence-and-uniqueness-b1.title: B1: Six-term determinants
exr-existence-and-uniqueness-b1.html: Using the Leibniz formula, listing all six terms, compute the determinants of A=(312104251),B=(1−1203142−2)∈M3(R). Then compute detA⊤ in the same way, and hence verify @thm-det-transpose for this A.

exr-existence-and-uniqueness-b2.title: B2: The determinant of \P_\sigma
exr-existence-and-uniqueness-b2.title_html: B2: The determinant of Pσ
exr-existence-and-uniqueness-b2.html:
Let σ∈Sn and let Pσ=(eσ(1)⋯eσ(n)) be its permutation matrix (@def-permutation-matrix).

  1. Prove that detPσ=sgn(σ).
  2. Hence compute det(001100010) and det(0100100000010010).

exr-existence-and-uniqueness-b3.title: B3: A zero row
exr-existence-and-uniqueness-b3.html: Let A∈Mn(F) have a zero row. Prove directly from @def-determinant, without using @thm-det-transpose, that detA=0. Then prove the same for a zero column.

exr-existence-and-uniqueness-c1.title: C1: Too many zeros
exr-existence-and-uniqueness-c1.html:
Let A∈Mn(F).

  1. Prove that if more than n2−n entries of A are zero, then detA=0.
  2. Show that the bound is sharp: give, for each n, a matrix with exactly n2−n zero entries and non-zero determinant.

exr-existence-and-uniqueness-c2.title: C2: Counting the cost
exr-existence-and-uniqueness-c2.html:
A computer performs about 109 multiplications per second.

  1. Show that evaluating the Leibniz formula term by term for an n×n matrix takes n!(n−1) multiplications. Estimate the time this takes for n=20.
  2. Gaussian elimination (Chapter 2) brings A to upper triangular form. Suppose no row swaps are needed. At step k (for k=1,…,n−1), each of the n−k rows below the pivot requires one division to find its multiplier and n−k multiplications to update its entries in columns k+1,…,n. Show that the total number of multiplications and divisions is (n−1)n(n+1)3, and evaluate it for n=20.

In the next section we will see that the determinant can be read off from this triangular form with n−1 further multiplications.

exr-existence-and-uniqueness-c3.title: C3: The permanent, and a change of field
exr-existence-and-uniqueness-c3.title_html: C3: The permanent, and a change of field
exr-existence-and-uniqueness-c3.html:
For A∈Mn(F) define perA=∑σ∈Snaσ(1)1⋯aσ(n)n.

  1. Prove that per is n-linear in the columns and perIn=1.
  2. Let n≥2. Prove that over R, per is not alternating.
  3. Prove that over F2, perA=detA for every A∈Mn(F2). Explain why this does not contradict (b) and @thm-alternating-form-uniqueness.

exr-minors-and-rank-a1.title: A1
exr-minors-and-rank-a1.html:
1. Define the k×k minor of A∈Mm×n(F) on rows I and columns J.
  2. True or false: if every principal minor of a square matrix is zero, the matrix is zero. Justify your answer.
  3. True or false: if A∈M4×5(F) has a non-zero 3×3 minor, then rankA≥3. Justify your answer.
  4. True or false: if A∈M3(F) has a zero 2×2 minor, then rankA≤1. Justify your answer.
  5. State the Cauchy–Binet formula, and say what it gives when m>n.
  6. Let A∈M2×3(R). Why is det(A⊤A)=0?

exr-minors-and-rank-b1.title: B1: Rank with a parameter
exr-minors-and-rank-b1.html: For s∈Q, let A(s)=(1s1s1111s). Use minors to find rankA(s) for every s.

exr-minors-and-rank-b2.title: B2: Checking Cauchy–Binet
exr-minors-and-rank-b2.html:
Let A=(102−111) and B=(21011−1) over Q.

  1. Compute det(AB) directly.
  2. Compute det(AB) by the Cauchy–Binet formula.
  3. Hence, without multiplying, find det(BA).

exr-minors-and-rank-b3.title: B3: The Lagrange identity
exr-minors-and-rank-b3.html:
Let a=(a1,…,an) and b=(b1,…,bn) be vectors in Rn, n≥2, and write a⋅b=∑iaibi.

  1. Let M∈M2×n(R) have rows a⊤ and b⊤. Compute MM⊤.
  2. Hence prove the Lagrange identity (a⋅a)(b⋅b)−(a⋅b)2=∑1≤i<j≤n(aibj−ajbi)2.
  3. Check it for a=(1,2,3) and b=(4,5,6), and deduce (a⋅b)2≤(a⋅a)(b⋅b) for all a,b∈Rn.

exr-minors-and-rank-c1.title: C1: Counting spanning trees
exr-minors-and-rank-c1.html:
Consider the network with vertices 1,2,3,4 and five edges, oriented as e1=1→2, e2=2→3, e3=3→4, e4=4→1, e5=1→3. A spanning tree is a set of 3 edges that connects all four vertices (ignoring orientation). Let N∈M4×5(R) be its incidence matrix (@def-incidence-matrix), let L=NN⊤, and let N0 and L0 be N and L with the row (and, for L, the column) of vertex 4 deleted.

  1. Compute L and detL0.
  2. List the spanning trees and count them.
  3. Show that L0=N0N0⊤, and use @cor-gram-determinant-nonnegative to write detL0 as a sum over 3-element sets of edges.
  4. Compute the minor of N0 for the tree {e1,e2,e3} and for the non-tree {e1,e2,e5}. Explain, for these two sets, why the answers are ±1 and 0.

The matrix-tree theorem says that for every connected network, detL0 equals the number of spanning trees; parts (c) and (d) are the heart of its proof, which Chapter 23 completes.

Hint: for (d), a set of edges containing a cycle gives dependent columns.

exr-minors-and-rank-c2.title: C2: Rank does not depend on the field
exr-minors-and-rank-c2.title_html: C2: Rank does not depend on the field
exr-minors-and-rank-c2.html:
Let K be a subfield of a field L (@def-restriction-of-scalars), and let A∈Mm×n(K). We may also regard A as a matrix in Mm×n(L).

  1. Explain why each minor detAI,J is the same element whether computed in K or in L.
  2. Prove that the rank of A over K equals its rank over L.
  3. Deduce: if a system Ax=0 with rational coefficients has a non-zero complex solution, it has a non-zero rational solution.

exr-multilinear-alternating-forms-a1.title: A1
exr-multilinear-alternating-forms-a1.html:
1. Define an alternating k-linear form on a vector space V over F.
  2. True or false: a bilinear form f on R2 with f(e1,e1)=f(e2,e2)=0 is alternating. Justify your answer.
  3. True or false: every skew-symmetric bilinear form on R5 is alternating. Justify your answer.
  4. Let f be an alternating 3-linear form on R3 and u,v∈R3. What is f(u,v,2u−v)?
  5. Name the move that proves an alternating form changes sign under a swap.

exr-multilinear-alternating-forms-b1.title: B1: Multilinear or Alternating?
exr-multilinear-alternating-forms-b1.html:
Determine which of the following functions are multilinear, and which of those are alternating. Justify your answer.

  1. R2×R2→R, (u,v)↦3u1v2−3u2v1.
  2. R2×R2→R, (u,v)↦u1v2−u2v1+1.
  3. R3×R3×R3→R, (u,v,w)↦u1v2w3.
  4. M2(R)×M2(R)→R, (A,B)↦tr(AB)−tr(BA).
  5. R[x]×R[x]→R, (p,q)↦p(1)q′(1)−p′(1)q(1).

exr-multilinear-alternating-forms-b2.title: B2: Alternating Bilinear Forms on F^2
exr-multilinear-alternating-forms-b2.title_html: B2: Alternating Bilinear Forms on F2
exr-multilinear-alternating-forms-b2.html: Let f be an alternating bilinear form on F2. Prove that f(u,v)=f(e1,e2)(u1v2−u2v1)for all u,v∈F2. Hence show that the alternating bilinear forms on F2 form a space of dimension 1.

exr-multilinear-alternating-forms-b3.title: B3: The Triple Product
exr-multilinear-alternating-forms-b3.html: For v,w∈R3 let v×w=(v2w3−v3w2, v3w1−v1w3, v1w2−v2w1), and define f(u,v,w)=u1(v×w)1+u2(v×w)2+u3(v×w)3. Show that f is an alternating 3-linear form on R3 with f(e1,e2,e3)=1.

exr-multilinear-alternating-forms-c1.title: C1: Too Many Arguments
exr-multilinear-alternating-forms-c1.html:
Let V be finite-dimensional with dim⁡V=n.

  1. Prove that every alternating k-linear form on V with k>n is the zero form.
  2. Deduce that the only alternating 3-linear form on F2 is zero, and give a non-zero alternating 2-linear form on F2 to show that the bound in (a) cannot be lowered to k≥n.

exr-multilinear-alternating-forms-c2.title: C2: Bilinear Forms over \nF_2
exr-multilinear-alternating-forms-c2.title_html: C2: Bilinear Forms over F2
exr-multilinear-alternating-forms-c2.html:
1. Let f be a bilinear form on F2 and write brs=f(er,es). Show that f(u,v)=∑r,s=12brsurvs, and that conversely every choice of four scalars brs defines a bilinear form this way. Hence there are exactly 16 bilinear forms on F22.
  2. Prove that a bilinear form on F22 is skew-symmetric if and only if b12=b21. How many are there?
  3. Prove that a bilinear form on F22 is alternating if and only if b11=b22=0 and b12=b21. How many are there?
  4. Over R, how do the analogous two sets of bilinear forms on R2 compare? Justify your answer.

exr-orientation-and-volume-a1.title: A1
exr-orientation-and-volume-a1.html:
1. State the definition of the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by a1,…,an∈Rn, and say what it is when the vectors are dependent.
  2. True or false: vol(a1+b,a2,…,an)=vol(a1,…,an)+vol(b,a2,…,an). Justify your answer.
  3. Which three rules characterize volume in @thm-volume-characterization?
  4. True or false: if detT=−2, then T doubles every volume. Justify your answer.
  5. Define “same orientation” for two ordered bases of a real vector space.
  6. True or false: for every n≥1, the map x↦−x on Rn reverses orientation. Justify your answer.

exr-orientation-and-volume-b1.title: B1: Volume of a parallelepiped
exr-orientation-and-volume-b1.html: Find the volume of the parallelepiped in R3 spanned by (2,1,0), (1,3,1) and (0,1,1). Hence find the volume of its image under the map T(x,y,z)=(x+y, y+z, 2z).

exr-orientation-and-volume-b2.title: B2: Comparing orientations
exr-orientation-and-volume-b2.html: In R3, let B=((1,1,0),(0,1,1),(1,0,1)), C=((0,1,0),(1,0,0),(1,1,1)) and D=((1,0,1),(1,1,0),(0,1,1)). Determine which pairs have the same orientation, and which are positively oriented. Justify your answer.

exr-orientation-and-volume-b3.title: B3: Areas of images
exr-orientation-and-volume-b3.html:
Let T(x,y)=(2x+y, −x+3y) on R2.

  1. Find the area of the image of the unit square under T.
  2. Find the area of the image of the parallelogram P((1,0),(1,2)), first by @thm-det-volume-scaling and then directly.
  3. Is T orientation-preserving?

exr-orientation-and-volume-c1.title: C1: Area of a triangle in space
exr-orientation-and-volume-c1.title_html: C1: Area of a triangle in space
exr-orientation-and-volume-c1.html:
For u,v∈R3, let A=(uv)∈M3×2(R). We define the area of the parallelogram P(u,v)⊆R3 to be det(A⊤A); Chapter 12 justifies this with inner products, where det(A⊤A) is recognized as a Gram determinant.

  1. Show that det(A⊤A)≥0, so the square root exists, and that det(A⊤A)=(u2v3−u3v2)2+(u3v1−u1v3)2+(u1v2−u2v1)2.
  2. Show that if u and v lie in the plane z=0, this area equals the area vol((u1,u2),(v1,v2)) of @def-parallelepiped-volume in R2.
  3. Find the area of the triangle with vertices (1,0,0), (0,2,0), (0,0,3).

Hint: apply @cor-gram-determinant-nonnegative to A⊤.

exr-orientation-and-volume-c2.title: C2: Rotations and reflections
exr-orientation-and-volume-c2.html:
For θ∈R, let Rθ=(cos⁡θ−sin⁡θsin⁡θcos⁡θ) (rotation by θ) and Sθ=(cos⁡2θsin⁡2θsin⁡2θ−cos⁡2θ) (reflection in the line through 0 at angle θ).

  1. Show that every rotation preserves orientation and area, and every reflection reverses orientation and preserves area.
  2. Show that SθSφ is orientation-preserving for all θ,φ. (It is in fact a rotation, but you need not show this.)
  3. Prove that no M∈M2(R) satisfies M2=S0=diag(1,−1). Does the same argument rule out M2=−I2?

exr-permutations-and-sign-a1.title: A1
exr-permutations-and-sign-a1.html:
1. Define an inversion of σ∈Sn and the sign sgnσ.
  2. True or false: every 3-cycle is odd. Justify your answer.
  3. True or false: some permutation is a product of 5 transpositions and also a product of 8 transpositions. Justify your answer.
  4. What is the kernel of sgn:Sn→{1,−1}? Is the set of odd permutations a subgroup?
  5. True or false: sgn(στ)=sgn(τσ) for all σ,τ∈Sn, even when στ≠τσ. Justify your answer.
  6. Let f be an alternating 3-linear form. Express f(v2,v3,v1) in terms of f(v1,v2,v3).

exr-permutations-and-sign-b1.title: B1: Computing Signs
exr-permutations-and-sign-b1.html:
Find the sign of each permutation, both by counting inversions and by using cycles.

  1. σ∈S4 with two-line notation (12342413).
  2. (1 2)(3 4 5)∈S5.
  3. (1 2 3)(2 3 4)∈S4.

exr-permutations-and-sign-b2.title: B2: Sign of the Inverse
exr-permutations-and-sign-b2.html: Prove that sgn(σ−1)=sgnσ for every σ∈Sn.

exr-permutations-and-sign-b3.title: B3: The Reversal Permutation
exr-permutations-and-sign-b3.html: Let ρ∈Sn be the reversal, ρ(i)=n+1−i. Show that inv(ρ)=n(n−1)/2. Hence find the n for which ρ is even, and decide the sign of ρ for n=6 and n=9.

exr-permutations-and-sign-c1.title: C1: Half the Permutations Are Even
exr-permutations-and-sign-c1.title_html: C1: Half the Permutations Are Even
exr-permutations-and-sign-c1.html:
Let n≥2. Prove that exactly n!/2 permutations in Sn are even.

Hint: consider σ↦(1 2)σ.

exr-permutations-and-sign-c2.title: C2: Sign from the Number of Cycles
exr-permutations-and-sign-c2.title_html: C2: Sign from the Number of Cycles
exr-permutations-and-sign-c2.html:
Suppose σ∈Sn is written as a product σ=γ1γ2⋯γc of disjoint cycles (no element appears in two of them) whose lengths k1,…,kc add up to n, where fixed points are included as cycles of length 1. (Such a product always exists: follow each element around its loop, as in @exm-cycle-notation.)

  1. Prove that sgnσ=(−1)n−c.
  2. Use (a) to find the sign of σ=(1 4 6)(2 5)∈S6, and compare with @exm-sign-two-ways.
  3. Deduce that an n-cycle in Sn and the identity in Sn have the same sign exactly when n is odd.

exr-properties-a1.title: A1
exr-properties-a1.html:
1. State how each of the three elementary row operations changes the determinant.
  2. True or false: the move R2→3R2−R1 does not change the determinant. Justify your answer.
  3. True or false: if A,B∈Mn(F) have detA=detB, then A and B are similar. Justify your answer.
  4. True or false: det(AB)=det(BA) for all A,B∈Mn(F). Justify your answer.
  5. Explain why detT does not depend on the basis used to compute it.
  6. Is det:Mn(F)→F a group homomorphism? Explain.

exr-properties-b1.title: B1: Determinants by elimination
exr-properties-b1.html: Compute the determinants of the following real matrices by row reduction, recording the effect of each operation. A=(120123140132−1125),B=(2−1314−273−22−146−395).

exr-properties-b2.title: B2: A parameter
exr-properties-b2.html: Let t∈R and At=(t111t111t). Find detAt as a factored polynomial in t. Hence determine for which t the matrix At is invertible.

exr-properties-b3.title: B3: The shift operator
exr-properties-b3.html: Let T:R[x]≤3→R[x]≤3, T(p)=p(x+1). Find detT. Hence show that T is invertible.

exr-properties-c1.title: C1: Orthogonal-type matrices
exr-properties-c1.html:
1. Let A∈Mn(R) satisfy A⊤A=In. Prove that detA=1 or detA=−1.
  2. Show that both values occur, for every n≥1.
  3. Over F2, what can detA be if A⊤A=In?

exr-properties-c2.title: C2: Left multiplication on matrices
exr-properties-c2.html:
Let A∈Mn(F), and let LA:Mn(F)→Mn(F), LA(X)=AX. This is a linear operator on a space of dimension n2. Prove that detLA=(detA)n.

  1. Order the matrix units column by column, B=(E11,E21,…,En1,E12,…,En2,…,E1n,…,Enn). Show that [LA]B consists of n copies of A placed along the diagonal, with zeros elsewhere.
  2. Show that LAB=LALB, and prove the formula when A is an elementary matrix.
  3. Prove the formula for invertible A, and then for non-invertible A.

Hint: for a swap matrix, identify [LPij]B as a permutation matrix and use @exr-existence-and-uniqueness-b2.

exr-properties-c3.title: C3: Non-square factors
exr-properties-c3.html:
1. Give A∈M2×1(R) and B∈M1×2(R) with det(BA)≠det(AB).
  2. Let m>n, A∈Mm×n(F) and B∈Mn×m(F). Prove that det(AB)=0.
  3. Explain why (a) does not contradict @thm-det-multiplicative.

exr-special-determinants-a1.title: A1
exr-special-determinants-a1.html:
1. State the Vandermonde determinant formula, including the order of the factors.
  2. True or false: V(x1,…,xn) is invertible whenever x1,…,xn are non-zero. Justify your answer.
  3. Write down the recurrence for the determinant of a tridiagonal matrix, and say which row the proof expands along.
  4. True or false: det(ABCD)=detAdetD whenever A and D are square and B=0. Justify your answer.
  5. True or false: det(In+uv⊤)=det(In+vu⊤) for all u,v∈Fn. Justify your answer.

exr-special-determinants-b1.title: B1: A 4 \times 4 Vandermonde determinant
exr-special-determinants-b1.title_html: B1: A 4×4 Vandermonde determinant
exr-special-determinants-b1.html: Compute det(1−11−1100011111248). Hence decide whether there is exactly one polynomial p∈R[x]≤3 with p(−1)=3, p(0)=1, p(1)=0, p(2)=5.

exr-special-determinants-b2.title: B2: The second-difference matrix
exr-special-determinants-b2.html: Let Kn∈Mn(R) have 2 on the diagonal, −1 directly above and below it, and 0 elsewhere. Prove that detKn=n+1. Hence show that Kn is invertible for every n.

exr-special-determinants-b3.title: B3: A rank-one update
exr-special-determinants-b3.html:
Let u=(1,2,3) and v=(1,−1,2) in Q3.

  1. Use @thm-matrix-determinant-lemma to find det(I3+uv⊤).
  2. Write out I3+uv⊤ and check your answer by elimination.
  3. Find all t∈Q for which I3+tuv⊤ is not invertible.

exr-special-determinants-c1.title: C1: The Cauchy determinant
exr-special-determinants-c1.html:
Let x1,…,xn,y1,…,yn∈F with xi+yj≠0 for all i,j, and let Qn∈Mn(F) have (i,j)-entry 1xi+yj. The goal is detQn=∏1≤i<j≤n(xj−xi)(yj−yi)∏i=1n∏j=1n(xi+yj).

  1. For i<n, subtract row n from row i. Show that the new (i,j)-entry is xn−xi(xi+yj)(xn+yj), and deduce that detQn=∏i<n(xn−xi)∏j(xn+yj)detQ′, where Q′ agrees with Qn in rows 1,…,n−1 and has last row (1,…,1).
  2. In Q′, for j<n, subtract column n from column j. Deduce that detQ′=∏j<n(yn−yj)∏i<n(xi+yn)detQn−1, where Qn−1 is built from x1,…,xn−1 and y1,…,yn−1.
  3. Prove the formula by induction on n.
  4. The Hilbert matrix Hn has (i,j)-entry 1i+j−1. Show that it is a Cauchy matrix, and use (c) to compute detH3.

Hint: in (a) and (b), factor scalars out of whole rows and columns using multilinearity.

exr-special-determinants-c2.title: C2: A circulant determinant over \nC
exr-special-determinants-c2.title_html: C2: A circulant determinant over C
exr-special-determinants-c2.html:
Let a,b,c∈C, let ω=e2πi/3, and let Z=(abccabbca).

  1. For k=0,1,2, let wk=(1,ωk,ω2k) and λk=a+bωk+cω2k. Show that Zwk=λkwk.
  2. Let W be the matrix with columns w0,w1,w2. Show that ZW=Wdiag(λ0,λ1,λ2) and that detW≠0. Deduce detZ=λ0λ1λ2.
  3. Using ω3=1 and 1+ω+ω2=0, deduce detZ=a3+b3+c3−3abc, and check this against the Leibniz formula.

Circulant matrices of every size are treated in Chapter 11.

exr-special-determinants-c3.title: C3: Rank-one updates of an invertible matrix
exr-special-determinants-c3.title_html: C3: Rank-one updates of an invertible matrix
exr-special-determinants-c3.html:
Let A∈Mn(F) be invertible and u,v∈Fn.

  1. Prove that det(A+uv⊤)=detA(1+v⊤A−1u).
  2. Deduce that A+uv⊤ is invertible if and only if v⊤A−1u≠−1.
  3. Give an example over Q with n=2 where A is invertible, uv⊤≠0, and A+uv⊤ is not invertible.

lem-alternating-permute-arguments.title: Permuting the arguments of an alternating form
lem-alternating-permute-arguments.title_html: Permuting the arguments of an alternating form
lem-alternating-permute-arguments.html: Let f be an alternating n-linear form on a vector space V over F, let v1,…,vn∈V, and let σ∈Sn. Then f(vσ(1),vσ(2),…,vσ(n))=sgn(σ)f(v1,v2,…,vn).

lem-charpoly-evaluation.title: Evaluating the Characteristic Polynomial
lem-charpoly-evaluation.html: Let A∈Mn(F) and c∈F. Then pA(c)=det(cIn−A).

prp-orientation-preserving.title: Determinant Sign and Orientation
prp-orientation-preserving.html: Let V be a vector space over R with dim⁡V=n≥1, let T∈L(V) be invertible, and let B=(v1,…,vn) be any basis of V. Then TB=(Tv1,…,Tvn) is a basis of V, and [id]TBB=[T]B. Hence B and TB have the same orientation if and only if detT>0, and this does not depend on B.

prp-sign-of-cycle.title: Sign of a Cycle
prp-sign-of-cycle.html: A k-cycle has sign (−1)k−1. In particular, cycles of even length are odd and cycles of odd length are even.

thm-adjugate-identity.title: The Adjugate Identity
thm-adjugate-identity.html: For every A∈Mn(F), AadjA=adjAA=(detA)In.

thm-alternating-form-uniqueness.title: Uniqueness of Alternating Forms
thm-alternating-form-uniqueness.html: Let f be an alternating n-linear form on Fn, and let a1,…,an∈Fn have entries aij as above. Then f(a1,…,an)=f(e1,…,en)∑σ∈Snsgn(σ)aσ(1)1aσ(2)2⋯aσ(n)n. In particular, an alternating n-linear form on Fn is determined by the single value f(e1,…,en).

thm-alternating-forms-space.title: Alternating Forms Form a Vector Space
thm-alternating-forms-space.title_html: Alternating Forms Form a Vector Space
thm-alternating-forms-space.html: The k-linear forms on V form a subspace of the vector space FVk of all functions Vk→F, with the pointwise operations of @exm-vector-spaces (d). The alternating k-linear forms on V form a subspace of it. In particular, both are vector spaces over F.

thm-alternating-properties.title: Properties of Alternating Forms
thm-alternating-properties.html:
Let f:Vk→F be an alternating k-linear form, let v1,…,vk∈V, and let i≠j be positions in {1,…,k}.

  1. (Swap) Exchanging the arguments in positions i and j multiplies f(v1,…,vk) by −1. In particular, f is skew-symmetric.
  2. (Shear) For every c∈F, replacing vi by vi+cvj does not change f(v1,…,vk).
  3. (Scaling) For every c∈F, replacing vi by cvi multiplies f(v1,…,vk) by c.
  4. (Dependence) If the list (v1,…,vk) is linearly dependent, then f(v1,…,vk)=0. In particular, f(v1,…,vk)=0 if some vi=0.

thm-cauchy-binet.title: Cauchy–Binet Formula
thm-cauchy-binet.html:
Let A∈Mm×n(F) and B∈Mn×m(F). Then det(AB)=∑S⊆[n]|S|=mdetA[m],SdetBS,[m], the sum running over all m-element subsets S of [n]. In particular:

  1. if m>n, the sum is empty and det(AB)=0;
  2. if m=n, the only subset is S=[n] and the formula is det(AB)=detAdetB.

thm-charpoly-coefficients.title: Coefficients of the Characteristic Polynomial
thm-charpoly-coefficients.html: Let n≥1 and A∈Mn(F). Then pA is monic of degree n, and pA(x)=xn−(trA)xn−1+⋯+(−1)ndetA, that is, the coefficient of xn−1 is −trA and the constant term is (−1)ndetA. (For n=1 these two statements concern the same coefficient, and both say it is −a11.)

thm-charpoly-root-iff-singular.title: Roots of the Characteristic Polynomial
thm-charpoly-root-iff-singular.html:
Let A∈Mn(F) with n≥1, and let c∈F.

  1. The following are equivalent: (i) pA(c)=0; (ii) cI−A is not invertible; (iii) there is a non-zero v∈Fn with Av=cv.
  2. There are at most n scalars c∈F with these properties.

thm-charpoly-similarity-invariant.title: Similar Matrices Have the Same Characteristic Polynomial
thm-charpoly-similarity-invariant.title_html: Similar Matrices Have the Same Characteristic Polynomial
thm-charpoly-similarity-invariant.html: If A,B∈Mn(F) are similar, then pA=pB.

thm-cramers-rule.title: Cramer’s Rule
thm-cramers-rule.html: Let A∈Mn(F) be invertible and b∈Fn. The unique solution x of Ax=b is given by xk=detAk(b)detA,k=1,…,n.

thm-det-block-triangular.title: Block Triangular Determinant
thm-det-block-triangular.html: Let A∈Mk(F), D∈Ml(F) and B∈Mk×l(F), with k,l≥1. Then det(AB0D)=detA⋅detD, where 0 is the l×k zero matrix. The same holds for (A0CD) with C∈Ml×k(F).

thm-det-homomorphism.title: The Determinant Is a Group Homomorphism
thm-det-homomorphism.title_html: The Determinant Is a Group Homomorphism
thm-det-homomorphism.html: Let n≥1. The determinant restricts to a surjective group homomorphism det:GLn(F)→F∖{0}. Its kernel is the special linear group SLn(F):={A∈Mn(F):detA=1}, which is therefore a subgroup of GLn(F).

thm-det-multiplicative.title: Multiplicativity of the Determinant
thm-det-multiplicative.html: For all A,B∈Mn(F), det(AB)=detAdetB.

thm-det-nonzero-iff-invertible.title: Invertible if and only if Non-Zero Determinant
thm-det-nonzero-iff-invertible.title_html: Invertible if and only if Non-Zero Determinant
thm-det-nonzero-iff-invertible.html: A matrix A∈Mn(F) is invertible if and only if detA≠0.

thm-det-operator-properties.title: Properties of the Determinant of an Operator
thm-det-operator-properties.title_html: Properties of the Determinant of an Operator
thm-det-operator-properties.html: Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over F and S,T∈L(V). Then det(ST)=detSdetT,detidV=1, and T is invertible if and only if detT≠0.

thm-det-properties.title: Properties of Determinants
thm-det-properties.html:
Let A,B∈Mn(F). Then:

  1. det(AB)=detAdetB;
  2. detA⊤=detA.

thm-det-row-operations.title: Row Operations and the Determinant
thm-det-row-operations.html:
Let A∈Mn(F) and let B be obtained from A by one operation.

  1. (Swap) If B is obtained by Ri↔Rj with i≠j, then detB=−detA.
  2. (Scale) If B is obtained by Ri→cRi with c∈F, then detB=cdetA.
  3. (Replace) If B is obtained by Ri→Ri+cRj with i≠j and c∈F, then detB=detA.
  4. The same three statements hold for the corresponding operations on columns.
  5. For the elementary matrices of @def-elementary-matrix, detPij=−1,detDi(c)=c,det(In+cEij)=1(i≠j), and det(EA)=detEdetA for every elementary matrix E∈Mn(F).

thm-det-transpose.title: Determinant of the Transpose
thm-det-transpose.html: For every A∈Mn(F), detA⊤=detA. Consequently, detA is also an alternating n-linear function of the rows of A, with value 1 at In.

thm-det-triangular.title: Determinant of a Triangular Matrix
thm-det-triangular.html: If A∈Mn(F) is upper triangular or lower triangular, then detA=a11a22⋯ann.

thm-det-volume-scaling.title: Linear Maps Scale Volume by \lvert \det \rvert
thm-det-volume-scaling.title_html: Linear Maps Scale Volume by |det|
thm-det-volume-scaling.html: Let T∈L(Rn) and a1,…,an∈Rn. Then vol(Ta1,…,Tan)=|detT|⋅vol(a1,…,an). In particular, the image of the unit cube under T has volume |detT|.

thm-invertible-tfae-det.title: Invertible Matrix Theorem, with Determinants
thm-invertible-tfae-det.html:
Let A∈Mn(F) and TA:Fn→Fn, x↦Ax. The following are equivalent, and each is equivalent to each of the eight conditions of @thm-invertible-tfae.

  1. A is invertible.
  2. TA is injective.
  3. TA is surjective.
  4. rankA=n.
  5. A⊤ is invertible.
  6. The rows of A are linearly independent.
  7. detA≠0.

thm-laplace-expansion.title: Laplace Expansion
thm-laplace-expansion.html:
Let n≥2 and A∈Mn(F), with cofactors Cij.

  1. (Along column j) For each j∈{1,…,n}, detA=a1jC1j+a2jC2j+⋯+anjCnj=∑i=1naijCij.
  2. (Along row i) For each i∈{1,…,n}, detA=ai1Ci1+ai2Ci2+⋯+ainCin=∑j=1naijCij.

thm-leibniz-formula-alternating.title: Existence: the Leibniz Formula
thm-leibniz-formula-alternating.html: Define D:Fn×⋯×Fn→F by D(a1,…,an)=∑σ∈Snsgn(σ)aσ(1)1aσ(2)2⋯aσ(n)n, where aij is the i-th entry of aj. Then D is an alternating n-linear form on Fn, and D(e1,…,en)=1.

thm-matrix-determinant-lemma.title: Matrix Determinant Lemma
thm-matrix-determinant-lemma.html: Let u,v∈Fn. Then det(In+uv⊤)=1+v⊤u.

thm-rank-via-minors.title: Rank via Minors
thm-rank-via-minors.html:
Let A∈Mm×n(F) be non-zero.

  1. rankA is the largest integer k such that A has a non-zero k×k minor.
  2. Equivalently, for each 1≤k≤min(m,n): rankA≥k if and only if some k×k minor of A is non-zero; and rankA<k if and only if every k×k minor of A is zero.

thm-sign-multiplicative.title: The Sign Is Multiplicative
thm-sign-multiplicative.html: For all σ,τ∈Sn, sgn(στ)=sgnσ⋅sgnτ.

thm-skew-symmetric-alternating.title: Skew-Symmetric and Alternating Forms
thm-skew-symmetric-alternating.html:
Let f:Vk→F be a k-linear form.

  1. If f is alternating, then f is skew-symmetric.
  2. If f is skew-symmetric and the characteristic of F is not 2, then f is alternating.

thm-tridiagonal-recurrence.title: Tridiagonal Recurrence
thm-tridiagonal-recurrence.html: With this notation, D1=a1, and for 2≤k≤n, Dk=akDk−1−bk−1ck−1Dk−2.

thm-two-orientations.title: There Are Exactly Two Orientations
thm-two-orientations.html:
Let V be a vector space over R with dim⁡V=n≥1.

  1. “Having the same orientation” is an equivalence relation on the set of ordered bases of V.
  2. It has exactly two equivalence classes. If B=(v1,…,vn), then B−=(−v1,v2,…,vn) lies in the class not containing B.

thm-vandermonde-determinant.title: Vandermonde Determinant
thm-vandermonde-determinant.html: Let n≥1 and x1,…,xn∈F. Then detV(x1,…,xn)=∏1≤i<j≤n(xj−xi), where the empty product (for n=1) is 1.

thm-volume-characterization.title: Volume Is Determined by Its Rules
thm-volume-characterization.title_html: Volume Is Determined by Its Rules
thm-volume-characterization.html:
Let n≥1, and let g be a function assigning a real number g(a1,…,an) to every list of n vectors in Rn. Suppose that for every list, every i≠j and every c∈R:

  1. g(a1,…,cai,…,an)=|c|g(a1,…,ai,…,an) (only slot i changes);
  2. g(a1,…,ai+caj,…,an)=g(a1,…,ai,…,an) (only slot i changes);
  3. g(e1,…,en)=1.

Then g(a1,…,an)=vol(a1,…,an) for every list. Moreover, vol itself satisfies (V1)–(V3).
